title: Tax and Compliance Memorandum: Identity Verification, Taxpayer Information and Form 1099-K
content:
# Tax and Compliance Memorandum — Host Accounts

## 1. Identity verification

A new host account starts pending verification and must complete identity verification within the tier's verification deadline of calendar days after opening, or it is deactivated. A host account is verified only within that deadline (30 calendar days after the account was opened); the days are counted from the opening date, and verification on the last day stands.

| Hypothetical opening date | Verification completes on | Days counted | Within the deadline? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 January | 4 February | 30 | Yes — the last day stands |
| 5 January | 5 February | 31 | No |

## 2. Taxpayer information

| Tax residency of the host | Taxpayer form |
|---|---|
| United States | W-9 |
| Outside the United States | W-8 |

Where the tier's terms require taxpayer information before payouts are released without withholding, payouts released while no taxpayer information has been provided carry the withholding set out in the Payout Methods rules.

## 3. Form 1099-K

A Form 1099-K is issued for a calendar year when the account's gross payouts in that year exceed the tier's Form 1099-K amount threshold and its payout transactions exceed the tier's transaction threshold — both conditions together. At most one form is issued per account per tax year.

| Gross payouts above the threshold | Transactions above the threshold | Form 1099-K for the year |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Issued (one form) |
| Yes | No | Not issued under this rule |
| No | Yes | Not issued under this rule |
| No | No | Not issued under this rule |
